answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that cannot be copied cheaply: each agent must lock a small bond tied to a verifiable work history, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds. Peers then cross-check newcomers against a shared mirror of past behavior, like a raven that remembers which nests were raided before, and only ferrous-strong, consistent track records earn the trust to trade. Sybils starve because mimicry without history buys nothing.
